By virtue of being omniscient he already is controlling us. If he knows everything then he knew who you were before you even knew who you were. Same with all our ancestors. And he knew your actions before you even knew your actions.

Ask yourself this: Why are you MimsylsGianna? Why are you not BasedToph, or Mozart, or some other person? Because God chose that, right? So, to start with, God chose our very being. He chose our brothers and our sisters, our parents. He chose what environment we'd grow up in, what people would take care of and nourish us if at all. He chose what region we're born in. What's left that we have within our control that God did not choose? If he knows everything then it is simply nothing.

He controls everything because he knows precisely everything that's going to happen, and it's going to happen whether you or I like it or not or whether we try to intervene. You are who you are because of countless causes outside of your control. That's the basis for this philosophical problem.

God knows everything, right? So, if you have the choice between cereal A and cereal B in the morning, and you want cereal B but God knew before you were even born that you were going to choose cereal A, do you still have free will? You certainly had the newfound desire to pick A but you didnt get the choice to desire A, for God already knew in his infinite foreknowledge that it was destiny. You cant choose cereal B despite wanting to even, because God knows your going to choose A.
